03 / THE SIFT STANDARD

Curiosity.
With receipts.

A match is a starting point for research. It doesn’t establish safety or predict a profit.

Read our approach ↗
01

Unknown means unknown.

Missing data never passes a required check. Coverage and freshness limits belong in the report.

02

Suspicion isn’t confirmation.

Bundle and wallet coordination analysis remain unsupported. When supported, suspected activity must be separated from confirmed evidence.

03

A transfer isn’t a sale.

Developer activity needs verified attribution and transaction evidence. It is not inferred from a market chart.

04

You stay in control.

Your rules require approval. Your wallet stays yours. Sift never executes trades or asks for private keys.

05 / THE BUILD, IN THE OPEN

Small steps.
Real progress.

Sift is in private testing.
Here’s what that means today.

IN THE PRIVATE TEST

  • Telegram commands and manual Solana checks
  • Guided criteria, review and saved rules
  • Discovery for approved, supported market rules
  • Fixed-pool market monitoring and controls
  • Limited liquidity account observations

Discovery coverage is limited. Monitoring setup and subsequent checks have been observed live; threshold alerts and restart recovery still need live validation.

STILL IN DEVELOPMENT

  • Conversational AI interpretation
  • Verified liquidity protection and timed locks
  • Developer attribution, holdings and sales
  • Reliable bundle and coordinated-buy analysis
  • A personal website dashboard

Unsupported requirements stay unresolved. Account observations do not verify a lock or full liquidity protection.

06 / A LITTLE MORE CONTEXT

Before you
head in.

Can I use Sift right now?+

The Telegram bot is in private testing with approved accounts. You can open it, but tester access is limited. Public access and pricing remain undecided.

Is an AI choosing my trades?+

No. Sift does not trade. The current bot uses guided setup and explicit market rules. AI interpretation of natural-language instructions is planned and not connected yet.

Where does the data come from?+

The private test uses DEX Screener market data, a limited GeckoTerminal Solana new-pools feed, and Solana RPC for supported account observations. Some tokens and venues may be missed. Reports show source coverage and unknown information.

Does monitoring run all the time?+

Only while the bot process is running and the monitor is active. Provider limits, pauses and downtime can delay checks or miss changes. Continuous hosting is not yet established.

Where can I follow the project?+

Our GitBook documentation explains the product, evidence standards and development direction. We’ll keep updating it as Sift develops.
